items_missed: 1_set_agenda: Never asked 'how are you today,' never gave an agenda statement (what we'd cover + rough time), never got an explicit 'sound good?'; the customer's name wasn't collected until the very last moment of the call.

2_probe: Only home size (two-bedroom condo) was gathered. No address/zip, no stairs or floors, no additional rooms, no special considerations, no boxes count, no storage question, no additional stops, no access/HOA/elevator question despite it being a high-rise, and no moving-stressors question.

3_pricing: No full 'what's included' rundown (gas, truck, taxes, tools), no disassembly/reassembly mention, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, and no full no-hidden-fees pitch (credit card fees, fuel surcharge, assembly fees).
4_clock: No mention that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, no 2.5-hour minimum, and no explicit sense-check ('does that make sense?').
5_estimate: No specialty-items question, no additional-stops variable, no walk-distance variable, no equivalents (school bus reference, etc.), and no traffic variable.
6_save_your_ass: Section entirely skipped — no prep-before-move-day speech, no consolidation examples, no carload tip, no close.

7_quote_booking: No attempt to lock in the date, no deposit mention, no email handoff offered, no bolded-details promise, no 'reply with corrections' line, no final 'any other questions?', and no hours/contact info given.
8_politeness: Customer's name ('Jay') was used only once in the entire call — needs 3+.

9_bonus: No proactive FAQ coverage (all answers were reactive to Jay's questions), no rapport/humor moment, no budget-conscious framing, and the delivery was rambling and run-on rather than clear and well-paced.
top_strength: The insurance explanation was genuinely strong and honest — Landon laid out the 60-cents-per-pound baseline liability, the $2,000 No Worries Damage Coverage, and then proactively steered Jay toward his own homeowner's policy for high-value items ('it's usually better to just kind of get that insured privately'). He also showed initiative offering to check with the Tampa branch manager about squeezing in an extra day even though the truck looked unavailable.
coaching_note: This call skipped the structure almost entirely — Landon jumped straight into pricing without an agenda, without asking a single probing question beyond bedroom count, and never attempted to book the date or offer an email confirmation. Slow down and run the format: agenda up front, probe for the details that actually drive the estimate (address, stairs, access, boxes, stressors), and close every call with a concrete next step — either lock in the date or promise a confirmation email with next steps. Also watch the rambling; several answers ran long and looped back on themselves, which makes the pricing harder for the customer to follow.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and helpful throughout with a warm farewell, but rapport was minimal, the customer's name was barely used, and repeated filler phrases ('yeah, for sure, for sure') made the warmth feel more habitual than genuine.
